tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
tools.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

schema.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. base_version.description: Required when slug is given: the version id this publish replaces — echo the version get_artifact or read_artifact returned (or your last publish result's). Rejected with a conflict if it no longer names the live version, so concurrent edits are never silently overwritten. Omit when creating.

content.description: The complete HTML document, at most 16 MiB. Must sniff as text/html — begin it with <!DOCTYPE html>.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Leave it out to keep the current one. Pass one only when the user asks for a different version, or this server's answer says to. If the publish is rejected because the contract is yanked or out of the supported window, republish with an explicit "0.0.0" to clear the contract — omitting the argument is not a reliable recovery (the server may carry the stored contract forward, repeating the rejection).

deadline.description: Optional, rarely needed: by when pages still open on an OLDER version must have moved to this one — one word: now, 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d, or an ISO-8601 time at most 30 days ahead. Omit it for ordinary edits (open pages then move at their next quiet moment); it cannot be relaxed once published.

favicon.description: Optional legacy emoji marker; omit it.

icon.description: One short, generic word for the artifact's tab icon — a plain signifier of what it is, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map; not a product or brand name. Pass one when creating; omit when republishing to keep the current icon.

shared_live.description: States who the artifact you are republishing is already shared with, and changes nothing: its 'read' value from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result. Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. Rejected if it does not match the artifact's current value.

# Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | — (2K only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

## Rule 3: Determine Output Format BEFORE Generating
target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

## Rule 4: Identify the Use Case, Then Confirm with User
Determine which scenario below best matches, present a suggested plan to the user, and confirm before executing. When a request spans several scenarios (e.g. A then L), combine their steps and confirm the combined plan.

---

## Scenario A: 3D Printing (white model)
Trigger: user mentions print, slicer, figurine, miniature, statue, physical model — single-color.
Suggested flow:
1. Detect installed slicers (meshy_send_to_slicer, slicer_type:"auto") — present list, save for later
2. Generate an untextured model with target_formats:["obj"]: meshy_text_to_3d (preview), or meshy_image_to_3d with should_texture:false
3. Wait for completion
4. Optionally check printability (meshy_analyze_printability, free). If it reports errors, either repair with model_url = the generation task's OBJ URL (model_urls.obj) so the result stays OBJ — on that route pass printer_type and intended_print_longest_side_mm, since intended_print_height_mm only works with task / GLB input — or repair by the analyze task, then meshy_convert the repaired GLB to obj (1 credit). print_ready only fixes OBJ
5. Download the OBJ (the repair task's, if repaired) with print_ready=true and print_height_mm (local Z-up fix and scaling)

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

8	- G1 Owner wins: where two GDDs disagree on a value, field, unit or contract, the registry `source:` GDD wins and the other conforms. If the thing is unregistered, the PUBLISHER of the field/signal/value wins and the consumer conforms.
9	- G2 Specialist disagreements: follow the creative-director's stated resolution in that GDD's disagreements list. Where the CD said "the user should choose", take the CD's stated lean.
10	- G3 Carried-over blockers (flagged "still not fixed"/"carried over"): previous edits did not land. After each edit, Grep for the old wording and confirm it is gone everywhere in the GDD (body, examples, ACs, tuning tables, OQs).
11	- G4 ACs that contradict the GDD's own formulas: recompute from the formula at registry defaults; never weaken a formula to match an AC.
12	- G5 Division/overflow at boundaries: guard explicitly (e.g. avail == 0 -> share 0, everything unserved); state the guard in the formula and add a boundary AC.
13	
14	## Cross-cutting rulings (R)
15	- R1 Restore epoch (consequence of X8/D16). Save/Load OWNS `restore_epoch` as a persisted integer in the save slot header (u32, starts 0). On every restore (death restart or load), Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (atomic header-only write) BEFORE the first RUNNING tick, so reloading the same autosave twice, in-process or after a fresh process start, gives a new epoch each time. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as (T, world_seed, restore_epoch) — sim-visible, pure. The KERNEL (command-simulation-layer.md) owns the one derivation for threat draws, counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE x restore_epoch, and owns RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE (value 1048576 unchanged; registry_request: move its source from attention-system.md to command-simulation-layer.md, with attention, horror and save-load in referenced_by). The stream name hash stays cached and unchanged. Attention and Horror call the kernel derivation; neither defines its own. Graph physical failures and persisted counters never read the epoch. Determinism (G3/G4) is defined given (save bytes, restore_epoch): the same pair replays identically; tests pin the epoch. Required ACs: (i) two successive restores of the same save yield epochs e and e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) a fresh-process reload of the same slot also advances the epoch; (iii) same (save, epoch) pair -> identical draws. Save/Load's 'none of it able to alter the sim' is amended to exempt restore_epoch.
16	- R2 seq (kernel CR-4). The kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source); callers never choose it; `submit()` stays void (fire-and-forget). A caller may attach an opaque `correlation` field (int) that the kernel echoes unchanged in the result/rejection event. Player Controller keys pre-play tokens by `correlation`. Update the kernel seq ACs (L883, L892, L902-904) and PC-7 together.
17	- R3 Completion sentinel (kernel CR-19b). Every owner callable receives `ctx`; results flow through ctx, never the return value: validate reports via ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason); snapshot via ctx.put(payload); apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx). Every callable's only return is `return ctx.complete()` (a typed token). No `-> void` owner callables.
18	- R4 Mouse aim. The Player Controller's form is canonical: cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp - picture_centre) / k_eff, where f_q is the quantized camera position actually used for the frame. The Pipeline PUBLISHES f_q. Aim direction = cursor_aim_world - AIM_ORIGIN, with AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos) + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y) (ruling D10); remove the chest-based subtraction from the Pipeline's D.14b/D.7. Cursor units: the fixer must VERIFY the unit of the cursor source (e.g. Viewport.get_mouse_position() under the Pipeline's canvas_items stretch wiring (ii)) against docs/engine-reference/godot/ and the Pipeline's own wiring text, then make the label, the variable table and the divisor agree in both GDDs; if the reference cannot settle it, mark the unit claim [UNV] and add an in-engine verification AC.
19	- R5 Carry tell (consequence of X3). Owners: Attention owns the intake numbers and the ONE integrator (Attention's walk-in convention and tick accounting are canonical; Boarding quotes them); Boarding owns the live-choice acceptance (AC-BS-123) and its K definitions, stated with Attention's integrator; Derelict owns the route length (21-28 tiles, X3). Scope: the burden applies only to SALVAGE carry — an item carried that was picked up inside a non-home locus (derelict) — moving or standing, until dropped/installed/thrown; never to carrying at home or of the player's own kit. Pace-robustness, scoped to that salvage carry only: (a) while a salvage carry is held, attention decay is suspended (freezing with cargo is priced, per X3); (b) dropping and re-taking the same item grants no fresh TELL_REARM immunity (the rearm timer keys on the item, not the pickup). Attention may re-derive weights/theta within these scoped rules, but must NOT invent weights to force K3-K5 green: all values stay PLACEHOLDER, and if the live-choice margin cannot be shown on paper with honest numbers, AC-BS-123(d) is re-written as a spike gate (owner, the boarding spike, its pass line), which is the expected outcome.
20	- R6 Pod statuses (consequence of user ruling D60 "statuses run in the pod"). Suit's reading stands: the reserve drains, the cell drains while lit, source RESERVE. Web Map conforms: delete WM-17b's HOLD reading and close ASK-S2. Pillar-2 mitigation: the valve click plays only on the source TRANSITION edge (once when breath_src becomes RESERVE), never per run. Recompute every pod-leg figure from the registry's own leg formula at registry defaults (ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS default 45, not 180; the registry's formulas use 945 ticks per leg — verify in the registry before using) and state run counts with an explicit floor and a carried remainder so every "exactly N" oracle is an integer.
21	- R7 PD1 static spill bound (user ruling D31: 'static authored spill <= 24 px'). The bound stays 24 px — it is the user's number. The home ship's spine_corridor (computed 26 px) must be brought within it by Derelict Authoring (light placement, fixture position or corridor dressing — the least invasive change; show the recomputed s <= 24). Lighting's AC-LO-69 stays per-push BLOCKING.
22	- R8 Units of a request field shared by producer and consumer (e.g. Perception LEVEL vs Audio): G1 — the producer defines the unit; the consumer converts. State the unit in both GDDs with the conversion.
23	- R9 Undesigned dependencies (VS/Alpha systems with no GDD): not a blocker; keep them listed as "undesigned — provisional contract" with the interface this GDD assumes.
24	- R10 Pending-confirmation defaults and PLACEHOLDER values are not changed by these rulings unless a blocker shows them internally inconsistent.
25	- R11 X14 (reference machine) stays OPEN: never name or invent a reference machine, build type or spec anywhere.

15	## Summary
16	
17	The Attention System is the simulation of the web's regard for the ship: one global, integer-only level that rises with the light the crew burns, the noise they make, the power they draw and the depth they work at, and falls back toward a depth-set baseline when they show restraint. Crossing one threshold starts a seeded, escalating 15 to 30 second **tell** (sound in a structure-borne bed, filaments resolving at the lamp cone's edge, never a meter) that restraint can abort; if it is not aborted, a **breach** puts STRESS on the section where the crew was loudest and on everything welded to it, sweeps the home-ship's single beacon, and ends in a short silence. It owns the tell-window contract: no web-originated harm lands outside a told breach, which is how Pillars 2 and 3 become testable.
18	
19	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Feature` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Command & Simulation Layer (designed), Life-Support Graph (designed), Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query (designed), Player Controller & Input (designed), Save/Load & Versioned Format (designed), Suit & Equipment (designed; soft, none at MVP)`; neighbours designed after this GDD (rows refreshed in the 2026-10-27 consistency pass where asked): `Ship Body & Interior Physics, Web Map & Transit, Horror Entities, Sanity & Hallucination Rules, Adaptive Audio & Tells (Designed, adaptive-audio-and-tells.md)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: Modular Ship Assembly, Perception Filter, Boarding & Salvage, HUD & Suit Layer, In-World Instruments, Chart Table, Debug Overlay and Derelict Authoring are Designed too; a matching status does not mean matching contracts, see OQ-AT-28 for the contract-diff outcome)*
20	
21	## Overview
22	
23	The Attention System is the web's regard of the ship, as simulation. In one sentence: it is a scene-tree-free, integer-only `SIM` block, `attention.state`, advanced by one divisor-6 step hook, `attention.step`, that holds **one global attention level** which rises with the light the crew keeps burning, the noise they make, the power they draw and the depth they work at, falls back toward a depth-set baseline when they show restraint, and drives a four-phase breach machine, **CALM → TELL → BREACH → SUBSIDING**, whose second step, the tell, is a promise to the player: a window of 10 to 30 seconds, seeded and fixed at the moment the level crosses the threshold, in which the world escalates for as long as the crew stays loud and the player can still choose to be quiet *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
24	
25	**The data layer.** Stimuli reach the level by two paths and no others. *Pushed noise* arrives through one Class B mutator, `push_stimulus(kind, source_ref, class)`, from the Player Controller (gait classes, and one per-tick carry-burden class *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*), Interaction (tool and one-shot classes); Horror Entities never calls it (HE-36); Attention owns the unit table `U[class]`, and one walking tick of noise defines the unit (1 attention unit, AU). *Ordered reads* take light from the Emitter State's per-emitter list and power from the Life-Support Graph's `power_use(section_id)`; the Suit pushes nothing, and Attention never reads Audio. The level is held in milli-AU, integrates the three channels with one memory constant `TAU_ATT_TICKS`, and decays by a ceiling step toward the baseline `B`, so it always reaches `B` exactly. One threshold `ATT_THRESHOLD` (theta) with a hold band (theta_HOLD) starts and ends events. The machine's only writes to the world are two: M17 `deposit_trace(STRESS, ...)` at `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT`, and the `set_beacon` command. Everything else it does is **publish** `attention.view`, a SIM read view of integers that Lighting, Audio, Horror, Sanity, Save/Load and its own presenter read.
26	
27	**The player-facing effect.** The player never sees the level. They meet this system as the hull creaking, from everywhere and nowhere, and creaking again, a little sooner each time; as filaments at the very edge of their lamp's cone that were texture a moment ago and are now strands; as dust in the beam turning as if the air had been displaced. That is the **tell**, and its length is not shown. Inside it the player can do the one thing the web responds to, which is less: stand still and set the cutter and any cargo down (the real levers), and, helping a little, kill the chest lamp or open the breaker *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (the breaker saves about 2 seconds and its inrush on re-closing gives them back, so it is the least of these, F-25 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*). If the level falls under the hold band and stays there, the tell ends in nothing and the creaking stops (an abort). If it does not, the tell ends in a **breach**: the section where the crew was loudest, and every section welded to it, takes STRESS (worn hardware fails faster than a person can walk), the home-ship's single beacon sweeps red, and a short silence follows when it is over. The player can survive a breach, or leave it by pod; they cannot win it. Camera, controls, lamp and ambient light do not change in any phase.
28	
29	**The contract this GDD owns.** Every web-originated harm to the ship, and provisionally to a crew body, must land inside a told breach: a tell of at least `TELL_MIN_TICKS` (derived as `ticks_for_seconds(W_MIN_WARNING_S)`) that the player could perceive and could have aborted by restraint *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **Audio is the guaranteed channel**: the structure-borne bed reaches every living player whatever is lit. The visual channel exists while an eligible emitter is lit, so a player who is fully dark has the audio channel only (ART:954 accepts this). The levers that abort a tell do not weigh the same: **stopping movement and stopping the tool are the lever; darkness and power-down help a little** (F-25 lists the seconds each saves). The Graph's fairness gate covers *endogenous* losses only (LS-13); for every non-player source it states "must therefore be preceded by that system's own Pillar 2 tell". This GDD is that tell. It is written as a testable predicate, `tell_window_contract`, audited by a `TellAudit` ledger that exists as a test fixture before Horror Entities and Adaptive Audio are designed, and it discharges the Graph's review criterion at LSG:1063.
30	
31	**What the game loses without it.** The core loop's hinge ("Light, noise, power spikes and depth raise it; it is shown in the world; crossing a line flips the rhythm. Dread is feeling it come." — game concept, Core Loop) would be a flat spawn timer, which is the exact outcome Pillar 3's design test rejects, or a hidden threshold, which Pillar 2's design test rejects. Horror Entities would have no phase to act inside and no permission predicate to honour; Save/Load would have no tell to defer an autosave around; Lighting would have no tier to gutter on; Adaptive Audio would have no beat to sound; Sanity would have no true, unhideable event to measure a lie against. The core hypothesis (the two-rhythm boarding-and-breach loop is tense and absorbing for a 30-minute solo session) cannot be tested without it.
32	
33	**MVP scope.** One threshold, one tier of lamp tell, one locus rule, one breach content (STRESS plus beacon plus published phase; RUPTURE and GOUGE are Horror's), one noise-only push API, ring-1 baseline plus placeholder rows for rings 2 and 3, and a contract-only suppressant (no effect verb, and the item itself is out of the MVP start kit, user ruling X6) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Multiple tiers, per-ring thresholds, the suppressant verb, per-player attribution and rate-coupled tell length are Vertical Slice addenda and are named, not absorbed (AT-30); the per-ring light and power stimulus gain is a pillar-flagged Vertical Slice requirement on Depth Rings & Scarcity (AT-6); phantom tells and false calm are rejected by pillar, permanently (AT-17).
34	
35	**Index wording reconciled.** The index rationale (IDX Systems Enumeration bullet 17) is honoured with five corrections, each recorded as a refresh owed and never as an edit:
36	
37	| The index says | This GDD does | Why | Refresh owed |
38	|---|---|---|---|
39	| noise and power stimuli "pushed in by Graph, Suit, Interaction, Assembly and Horrors" | **two intake paths**: noise is pushed (Controller, Interaction; Horror pushes none and is not a declared caller, HE-36); light and power are *ordered reads* (`emitters()`, `power_use`); Suit and Assembly push nothing at MVP | the Graph publishes `power_use` as a read (LS-19); Suit declares "No stimuli pushed" (SE-31); Interaction already pushes LOUD at cut completion (IA-33), so an Assembly push would double count | index bullet 17 wording (C6); kernel Interactions row 4 (C7) |
40	| "flicker as a Lighting modifier" | the lamp effect is a **gutter**, published as a tier | Lighting bans the word for the tell (LO-19, LO-20) | index wording (C10) |
41	| "Lighting never reads Attention" (IDX soft-cycle note) | Lighting reads only the published tier and timing; Attention reads nothing Lighting produces | LO-20 supersedes it | index soft-cycle note (C12) |
42	| "baseline set by depth" | `B = B_table[ring]` of the deepest section holding a living player; per-ring values belong to Depth Rings (VS) | one deterministic rule; "loudest player" is undefined | none |
43	| Suit listed as a Hard dependency | Suit is **soft, none at MVP**: contract text for the suppressant only | Suit pushes nothing and Attention reads nothing of it | index edge Attention → Suit (C14) |
44	
45	**Reading guide.** Detailed Design holds the thirty-odd named rules `AT-1` to `AT-32` (Core Rules), the state machine, and one Interactions table per neighbour. Numbers in this document are `[PLACEHOLDER]` unless a registry name says otherwise; every locked constant (`TICK_RATE`, `W_MIN_WARNING_S`, `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT`, `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS`, `NOISE_PER_TICK`, `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`, `MAX_EMITTERS`, `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP`, `AUTOSAVE_*`, `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS`, `MOD_FLOOR_PM`) is cited by name and never restated with a number of this document's own. Lighting's **`gutter_recipe` bounds** (its variables `G_LO` and `G_HI`, tier 1 at 480 and 960 frames, REG:2187-2188, registry `gutter_recipe` variables) are not registry entries: they are cited as "Lighting's `gutter_recipe` bounds" and take no `referenced_by` from this document (C24).
46	
47	**Implementation digest** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(one page for story authors; the rule ids carry the detail and where this digest and a rule differ, the rule wins).* (1) *Shape:* one `SIM` block `attention.state` (WORLD, SHARED, schema 1) and one hook `attention.step` at divisor 6, offset 0, `after [graph.propagate.power, emitter.place]`; integer-only; the only `rng_derive` is the tell draw (AT-1, AT-28). (2) *Intake:* noise by `push_stimulus(NOISE, source, class)` from the Controller and Interaction only (the Controller also pushes one per-tick carry-burden class, F-26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, attributed to a section at push time into `pending_noise_mAU` and `pending_ledger_mAU[s]`; light from `emitters()`; power from `power_use` as `W_P × nl_w` plus `W_S ×` a lamp-excluded five-run delta from Attention's own `nl_hist_w` (AT-3, AT-4, F-1 to F-4). (3) *Level:* `L' = clamp(L + I_run − dec, B, L_CEIL)` with `dec = ceil(6 (L − B) / tau)`, and `dec = 0` on a run in which a salvage carry was held *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*; `B` from the deepest living seat's ring (AT-5, AT-6, F-5, F-8). (4) *Machine:* CALM to TELL (at `L ≥ theta`, past both timers), TELL to BREACH (due run, `L ≥ theta_HOLD`, not `locus_vacated`), BREACH to SUBSIDING to CALM; TELL to CALM on an abort (twenty runs under the hold line, or at the due run under it, or the departure void) (AT-7 to AT-13, AT-22). (5) *Tell:* length drawn once (900 to 1800 ticks, floor 600 on every path) under a key that changes per restore epoch; beats on a hash schedule whose interval and tier follow a behaviour-keyed escalation clock (frozen while `L < theta_HOLD`) with one counter for both senses; nothing published reveals the end (AT-8, AT-9, AT-16) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. (6) *Breach:* STRESS on the locus body in bursts, `set_beacon` at T+1; light and power feed the locus ledger through their own sections and noise dominates it (AT-11, AT-12, AT-14, AT-18, F-6) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. (7) *Contract:* `exogenous_permitted(section)` and the `TellAudit` replay are the testable form of Pillars 2 and 3 (AT-15, F-23). (8) *Persisted:* the field list in AT-1; every restore failure is a hard `ATTENTION_RESTORE_*` and nothing is clamped. (9) *Lints that gate data:* F-15 and F-15b abortability (rows `x_dark`, `x_dark_home_lit`, `autonomous_transient`), F-16 dark floor, F-20 and F-21 autosave deferral, IR-1 to IR-3, IR-4 (`carry_decision`, F-26), the DOCK_STATUS budget (F-16), F-24 cue floor and rung width, the theta upper bound (F-5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. (10) *Not built here:* Horror's behaviours, Audio's sounds, Lighting's gutter, the suppressant verb, the per-ring gain (AT-30). **Provenance codes (key).** `Rn` and `CQ-n` are rulings and checkpoint questions of the 2026-10-26 authoring run, `CP-Cn` and `GD-n` are consistency-pass and game-designer findings, `Cn` rows are refreshes owed (Cross-References), `AF-n` are art flags and `Xn` are additions. The ruling files are not in the repository, so the rule text is authoritative and a code is only a pointer; moving rationale into a separate decision log is recorded in OQ-AT-28 and not done in this pass.
48	
49	## Player Fantasy
50	
51	**It noticed.** The Synaptic Sea's web does not hunt you; it *looks*, and what it looks by is what you do. Everything you do that is loud, bright or hungry is something it can see, and the acts do not weigh the same: a running step or a cut costs far more than a lamp *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Depth sets how closely it is already watching. Your choices move it from there.
52	
53	Most of the time you are in the boarding rhythm: still, dusty, deliberate, every door a decision about how loud to be. Then the hull creaks, and creaks again, from everywhere and nowhere. At the edge of your light, filaments that were only texture resolve into strands, and the dust in your beam turns as if something displaced the air. The creaks come closer together for as long as you stay loud, and nothing tells you when they will stop; go still and, once the web's regard has fallen back under its hold line, they stop quickening and hold where they are, because the signal is earned *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. That takes a while: 8 seconds after a full stop in the dark, about 12 with the lamp on and the home ship lit, and until then the creaks keep tightening, so a player who stops with the lamp on usually hears the tell reach its second tier before it holds *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the lag stated honestly, F-13, AC-AT-135)*. Your lamp, your hands and your view do not change. The ship does, and the web is leaning in. This is the tell: ten to thirty seconds that are yours.
54	
55	In that window, restraint is a real move. Stand still, set down the cutter and whatever you are hauling, and the web can lose interest; kill the lamp and open the breaker and it loses interest a little sooner *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The creaking stops and the strands sink back into texture. Or you decide the scrubber is worth it, finish the cut, and run for the pod while the section you stressed fails faster than you can walk. Leave, and the web lets go: the red beacon that swept the home-ship while the breach was on goes dark, and the wreck behind you goes on failing in silence. You did not win. You chose, and you can say afterwards what you heard and what you did about it.
56	
57	The tell never lies. Your sanity can show you a monster in the dark. It cannot fake the creak that comes before the web turns on the ship or on you, and it cannot hide it. When harm arrives without that warning, the first thing to doubt is your eyes. *(Crew-body scope provisional: Horror Entities must repeat AT-15 or surface a CONFLICT.)*
58	
59	**The emotion is being noticed, not being attacked.** The art bible names it: "It noticed. The small-animal feeling of being looked at. Not yet fear — attention." (ART 2.7). This system owns the gap between *noticed* and *fear*, and makes that gap the player's to spend. The power fantasy is the night-shift engineer's or the cave diver's: *I know what makes me loud, and I can choose to be quiet.* The player has no power over the web; their power is over their own emission. They never beat it. They go unnoticed, or they get through being noticed, or they leave.
60

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

13	> **User rulings (design-review decisions), 2026-10-27** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the user ruled "I agree with all of your recommendations on those decisions" and answered "yes to all" on the held list. **Resolved (user rulings):** OQ-AT-1 (an opt-in haptic pulse on beats, off by default; still no captions), OQ-AT-2 (BEACON `gates_actions` stays false), OQ-AT-5 (the MVP suppressant is out of the start kit; the contract names stay dormant), OQ-AT-12 (the departure void is confirmed; a home-ship-locus tell is not voidable by hopping and 'the lights you left on' is the price), OQ-AT-24 (derelict A passes by option (b)), OQ-AT-25 (escalation freezes while `L < theta_HOLD`, behaviour-keyed; the F-12 floor proof is redone), OQ-AT-27 (the lever against throttle play is the calibration route: a per-tick carry-burden intake, class `BURDEN`, F-26), OQ-AT-29 (threat draws re-key per restore epoch), OQ-AT-30 (the DOCK_STATUS pod glow is unswitchable light and never a tell carrier), OQ-AT-32 (statuses run in the pod and a death there is the Controller's DEAD). **Defaults applied, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20):** OQ-AT-23 (the berth is one `LOUD` push, Interaction's IA-40), OQ-AT-26 (neither abortability retune; the switches guarantee stands), OQ-AT-31 (the light stimulus is shape-blind by decision). **Not decided:** the reference machine behind AC-AT-54b and AC-AT-124 (X14) stays open and no machine is named in this document. The CD-GDD-ALIGN review above (2026-10-26) predates every one of these amendments.
14	
15	## Summary
16	
17	The Attention System is the simulation of the web's regard for the ship: one global, integer-only level that rises with the light the crew burns, the noise they make, the power they draw and the depth they work at, and falls back toward a depth-set baseline when they show restraint. Crossing one threshold starts a seeded, escalating 15 to 30 second **tell** (sound in a structure-borne bed, filaments resolving at the lamp cone's edge, never a meter) that restraint can abort; if it is not aborted, a **breach** puts STRESS on the section where the crew was loudest and on everything welded to it, sweeps the home-ship's single beacon, and ends in a short silence. It owns the tell-window contract: no web-originated harm lands outside a told breach, which is how Pillars 2 and 3 become testable.
18	
19	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Feature` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Command & Simulation Layer (designed), Life-Support Graph (designed), Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query (designed), Player Controller & Input (designed), Save/Load & Versioned Format (designed), Suit & Equipment (designed; soft, none at MVP)`; neighbours designed after this GDD (rows refreshed in the 2026-10-27 consistency pass where asked): `Ship Body & Interior Physics, Web Map & Transit, Horror Entities, Sanity & Hallucination Rules, Adaptive Audio & Tells (Designed, adaptive-audio-and-tells.md)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: Modular Ship Assembly, Perception Filter, Boarding & Salvage, HUD & Suit Layer, In-World Instruments, Chart Table, Debug Overlay and Derelict Authoring are Designed too; a matching status does not mean matching contracts, see OQ-AT-28 for the contract-diff outcome)*
20	
21	## Overview
22	
23	The Attention System is the web's regard of the ship, as simulation. In one sentence: it is a scene-tree-free, integer-only `SIM` block, `attention.state`, advanced by one divisor-6 step hook, `attention.step`, that holds **one global attention level** which rises with the light the crew keeps burning, the noise they make, the power they draw and the depth they work at, falls back toward a depth-set baseline when they show restraint, and drives a four-phase breach machine, **CALM → TELL → BREACH → SUBSIDING**, whose second step, the tell, is a promise to the player: a window of 10 to 30 seconds, seeded and fixed at the moment the level crosses the threshold, in which the world escalates for as long as the crew stays loud and the player can still choose to be quiet *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
24	
25	**The data layer.** Stimuli reach the level by two paths and no others. *Pushed noise* arrives through one Class B mutator, `push_stimulus(kind, source_ref, class)`, from the Player Controller (gait classes, and one per-tick carry-burden class *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*), Interaction (tool and one-shot classes); Horror Entities never calls it (HE-36); Attention owns the unit table `U[class]`, and one walking tick of noise defines the unit (1 attention unit, AU). *Ordered reads* take light from the Emitter State's per-emitter list and power from the Life-Support Graph's `power_use(section_id)`; the Suit pushes nothing, and Attention never reads Audio. The level is held in milli-AU, integrates the three channels with one memory constant `TAU_ATT_TICKS`, and decays by a ceiling step toward the baseline `B`, so it always reaches `B` exactly. One threshold `ATT_THRESHOLD` (theta) with a hold band (theta_HOLD) starts and ends events. The machine's only writes to the world are two: M17 `deposit_trace(STRESS, ...)` at `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT`, and the `set_beacon` command. Everything else it does is **publish** `attention.view`, a SIM read view of integers that Lighting, Audio, Horror, Sanity, Save/Load and its own presenter read.
26	
27	**The player-facing effect.** The player never sees the level. They meet this system as the hull creaking, from everywhere and nowhere, and creaking again, a little sooner each time; as filaments at the very edge of their lamp's cone that were texture a moment ago and are now strands; as dust in the beam turning as if the air had been displaced. That is the **tell**, and its length is not shown. Inside it the player can do the one thing the web responds to, which is less: stand still and set the cutter and any cargo down (the real levers), and, helping a little, kill the chest lamp or open the breaker *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (the breaker saves about 2 seconds and its inrush on re-closing gives them back, so it is the least of these, F-25 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*). If the level falls under the hold band and stays there, the tell ends in nothing and the creaking stops (an abort). If it does not, the tell ends in a **breach**: the section where the crew was loudest, and every section welded to it, takes STRESS (worn hardware fails faster than a person can walk), the home-ship's single beacon sweeps red, and a short silence follows when it is over. The player can survive a breach, or leave it by pod; they cannot win it. Camera, controls, lamp and ambient light do not change in any phase.
28	
29	**The contract this GDD owns.** Every web-originated harm to the ship, and provisionally to a crew body, must land inside a told breach: a tell of at least `TELL_MIN_TICKS` (derived as `ticks_for_seconds(W_MIN_WARNING_S)`) that the player could perceive and could have aborted by restraint *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **Audio is the guaranteed channel**: the structure-borne bed reaches every living player whatever is lit. The visual channel exists while an eligible emitter is lit, so a player who is fully dark has the audio channel only (ART:954 accepts this). The levers that abort a tell do not weigh the same: **stopping movement and stopping the tool are the lever; darkness and power-down help a little** (F-25 lists the seconds each saves). The Graph's fairness gate covers *endogenous* losses only (LS-13); for every non-player source it states "must therefore be preceded by that system's own Pillar 2 tell". This GDD is that tell. It is written as a testable predicate, `tell_window_contract`, audited by a `TellAudit` ledger that exists as a test fixture before Horror Entities and Adaptive Audio are designed, and it discharges the Graph's review criterion at LSG:1063.
30	
31	**What the game loses without it.** The core loop's hinge ("Light, noise, power spikes and depth raise it; it is shown in the world; crossing a line flips the rhythm. Dread is feeling it come." — game concept, Core Loop) would be a flat spawn timer, which is the exact outcome Pillar 3's design test rejects, or a hidden threshold, which Pillar 2's design test rejects. Horror Entities would have no phase to act inside and no permission predicate to honour; Save/Load would have no tell to defer an autosave around; Lighting would have no tier to gutter on; Adaptive Audio would have no beat to sound; Sanity would have no true, unhideable event to measure a lie against. The core hypothesis (the two-rhythm boarding-and-breach loop is tense and absorbing for a 30-minute solo session) cannot be tested without it.
32	
33	**MVP scope.** One threshold, one tier of lamp tell, one locus rule, one breach content (STRESS plus beacon plus published phase; RUPTURE and GOUGE are Horror's), one noise-only push API, ring-1 baseline plus placeholder rows for rings 2 and 3, and a contract-only suppressant (no effect verb, and the item itself is out of the MVP start kit, user ruling X6) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Multiple tiers, per-ring thresholds, the suppressant verb, per-player attribution and rate-coupled tell length are Vertical Slice addenda and are named, not absorbed (AT-30); the per-ring light and power stimulus gain is a pillar-flagged Vertical Slice requirement on Depth Rings & Scarcity (AT-6); phantom tells and false calm are rejected by pillar, permanently (AT-17).
34	
35	**Index wording reconciled.** The index rationale (IDX Systems Enumeration bullet 17) is honoured with five corrections, each recorded as a refresh owed and never as an edit:
36	
37	| The index says | This GDD does | Why | Refresh owed |
38	|---|---|---|---|
39	| noise and power stimuli "pushed in by Graph, Suit, Interaction, Assembly and Horrors" | **two intake paths**: noise is pushed (Controller, Interaction; Horror pushes none and is not a declared caller, HE-36); light and power are *ordered reads* (`emitters()`, `power_use`); Suit and Assembly push nothing at MVP | the Graph publishes `power_use` as a read (LS-19); Suit declares "No stimuli pushed" (SE-31); Interaction already pushes LOUD at cut completion (IA-33), so an Assembly push would double count | index bullet 17 wording (C6); kernel Interactions row 4 (C7) |
40	| "flicker as a Lighting modifier" | the lamp effect is a **gutter**, published as a tier | Lighting bans the word for the tell (LO-19, LO-20) | index wording (C10) |
41	| "Lighting never reads Attention" (IDX soft-cycle note) | Lighting reads only the published tier and timing; Attention reads nothing Lighting produces | LO-20 supersedes it | index soft-cycle note (C12) |
42	| "baseline set by depth" | `B = B_table[ring]` of the deepest section holding a living player; per-ring values belong to Depth Rings (VS) | one deterministic rule; "loudest player" is undefined | none |
43	| Suit listed as a Hard dependency | Suit is **soft, none at MVP**: contract text for the suppressant only | Suit pushes nothing and Attention reads nothing of it | index edge Attention → Suit (C14) |
44	
45	**Reading guide.** Detailed Design holds the thirty-odd named rules `AT-1` to `AT-32` (Core Rules), the state machine, and one Interactions table per neighbour. Numbers in this document are `[PLACEHOLDER]` unless a registry name says otherwise; every locked constant (`TICK_RATE`, `W_MIN_WARNING_S`, `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT`, `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS`, `NOISE_PER_TICK`, `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`, `MAX_EMITTERS`, `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP`, `AUTOSAVE_*`, `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS`, `MOD_FLOOR_PM`) is cited by name and never restated with a number of this document's own. Lighting's **`gutter_recipe` bounds** (its variables `G_LO` and `G_HI`, tier 1 at 480 and 960 frames, REG:2187-2188, registry `gutter_recipe` variables) are not registry entries: they are cited as "Lighting's `gutter_recipe` bounds" and take no `referenced_by` from this document (C24).
46	
47	**Implementation digest** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(one page for story authors; the rule ids carry the detail and where this digest and a rule differ, the rule wins).* (1) *Shape:* one `SIM` block `attention.state` (WORLD, SHARED, schema 1) and one hook `attention.step` at divisor 6, offset 0, `after [graph.propagate.power, emitter.place]`; integer-only; the only `rng_derive` is the tell draw (AT-1, AT-28). (2) *Intake:* noise by `push_stimulus(NOISE, source, class)` from the Controller and Interaction only (the Controller also pushes one per-tick carry-burden class, F-26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, attributed to a section at push time into `pending_noise_mAU` and `pending_ledger_mAU[s]`; light from `emitters()`; power from `power_use` as `W_P × nl_w` plus `W_S ×` a lamp-excluded five-run delta from Attention's own `nl_hist_w` (AT-3, AT-4, F-1 to F-4). (3) *Level:* `L' = clamp(L + I_run − dec, B, L_CEIL)` with `dec = ceil(6 (L − B) / tau)`, and `dec = 0` on a run in which a salvage carry was held *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*; `B` from the deepest living seat's ring (AT-5, AT-6, F-5, F-8). (4) *Machine:* CALM to TELL (at `L ≥ theta`, past both timers), TELL to BREACH (due run, `L ≥ theta_HOLD`, not `locus_vacated`), BREACH to SUBSIDING to CALM; TELL to CALM on an abort (twenty runs under the hold line, or at the due run under it, or the departure void) (AT-7 to AT-13, AT-22). (5) *Tell:* length drawn once (900 to 1800 ticks, floor 600 on every path) under a key that changes per restore epoch; beats on a hash schedule whose interval and tier follow a behaviour-keyed escalation clock (frozen while `L < theta_HOLD`) with one counter for both senses; nothing published reveals the end (AT-8, AT-9, AT-16) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. (6) *Breach:* STRESS on the locus body in bursts, `set_beacon` at T+1; light and power feed the locus ledger through their own sections and noise dominates it (AT-11, AT-12, AT-14, AT-18, F-6) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. (7) *Contract:* `exogenous_permitted(section)` and the `TellAudit` replay are the testable form of Pillars 2 and 3 (AT-15, F-23). (8) *Persisted:* the field list in AT-1; every restore failure is a hard `ATTENTION_RESTORE_*` and nothing is clamped. (9) *Lints that gate data:* F-15 and F-15b abortability (rows `x_dark`, `x_dark_home_lit`, `autonomous_transient`), F-16 dark floor, F-20 and F-21 autosave deferral, IR-1 to IR-3, IR-4 (`carry_decision`, F-26), the DOCK_STATUS budget (F-16), F-24 cue floor and rung width, the theta upper bound (F-5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. (10) *Not built here:* Horror's behaviours, Audio's sounds, Lighting's gutter, the suppressant verb, the per-ring gain (AT-30). **Provenance codes (key).** `Rn` and `CQ-n` are rulings and checkpoint questions of the 2026-10-26 authoring run, `CP-Cn` and `GD-n` are consistency-pass and game-designer findings, `Cn` rows are refreshes owed (Cross-References), `AF-n` are art flags and `Xn` are additions. The ruling files are not in the repository, so the rule text is authoritative and a code is only a pointer; moving rationale into a separate decision log is recorded in OQ-AT-28 and not done in this pass.
48	
49	## Player Fantasy
50	
51	**It noticed.** The Synaptic Sea's web does not hunt you; it *looks*, and what it looks by is what you do. Everything you do that is loud, bright or hungry is something it can see, and the acts do not weigh the same: a running step or a cut costs far more than a lamp *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Depth sets how closely it is already watching. Your choices move it from there.
52	
53	Most of the time you are in the boarding rhythm: still, dusty, deliberate, every door a decision about how loud to be. Then the hull creaks, and creaks again, from everywhere and nowhere. At the edge of your light, filaments that were only texture resolve into strands, and the dust in your beam turns as if something displaced the air. The creaks come closer together for as long as you stay loud, and nothing tells you when they will stop; go still and, once the web's regard has fallen back under its hold line, they stop quickening and hold where they are, because the signal is earned *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. That takes a while: 8 seconds after a full stop in the dark, about 12 with the lamp on and the home ship lit, and until then the creaks keep tightening, so a player who stops with the lamp on usually hears the tell reach its second tier before it holds *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the lag stated honestly, F-13, AC-AT-135)*. Your lamp, your hands and your view do not change. The ship does, and the web is leaning in. This is the tell: ten to thirty seconds that are yours.
54	
55	In that window, restraint is a real move. Stand still, set down the cutter and whatever you are hauling, and the web can lose interest; kill the lamp and open the breaker and it loses interest a little sooner *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The creaking stops and the strands sink back into texture. Or you decide the scrubber is worth it, finish the cut, and run for the pod while the section you stressed fails faster than you can walk. Leave, and the web lets go: the red beacon that swept the home-ship while the breach was on goes dark, and the wreck behind you goes on failing in silence. You did not win. You chose, and you can say afterwards what you heard and what you did about it.
56	
57	The tell never lies. Your sanity can show you a monster in the dark. It cannot fake the creak that comes before the web turns on the ship or on you, and it cannot hide it. When harm arrives without that warning, the first thing to doubt is your eyes. *(Crew-body scope provisional: Horror Entities must repeat AT-15 or surface a CONFLICT.)*
58	
59	**The emotion is being noticed, not being attacked.** The art bible names it: "It noticed. The small-animal feeling of being looked at. Not yet fear — attention." (ART 2.7). This system owns the gap between *noticed* and *fear*, and makes that gap the player's to spend. The power fantasy is the night-shift engineer's or the cave diver's: *I know what makes me loud, and I can choose to be quiet.* The player has no power over the web; their power is over their own emission. They never beat it. They go unnoticed, or they get through being noticed, or they leave.
60

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

The 8 GDD sections, in order:

3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled

=== 75
*Moment A, "I can leave now" (the abort, the Pillar 3 payoff).* Derelict A, ring 1. The player is partway through a salvage cut with two fixtures lit from a breaker they closed earlier. The level crosses `ATT_THRESHOLD`; a seeded tell begins. Beat 0 is a creak in the bed, audio first. Over the next beats two or three filaments at the cone's edge resolve into strands, and the dust turns. The player releases the channel (the partial is kept for `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`), stands still, kills the chest lamp and opens the breaker *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (the stop is what aborts the tell; the lamp and the breaker each shave about 2 seconds, and the breaker's inrush returns its 2 seconds when it is closed again, F-25 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*). The level falls under theta_HOLD and stays there for `ABORT_HOLD_TICKS`, or is under it at `breach_due_T`. Phase returns to CALM: no beacon, no STRESS, the beat stops. With the lamp off and the breaker open no lit region remains, so no filament is drawn at all (ART 3.3 / Principle 1). *An abort always forfeits the partial* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The earliest abort completes 594 ticks after the stop on a clean ship, 6 ticks (100 ms) inside `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`, a window no player can use, and 606 ticks with the two wake glows the MVP ships with, past it (F-15b) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and with the home ship lit it completes later still; the cut restarts from zero. That is the price of restraint, stated plainly and chosen on purpose, and the breach that has teeth (AT-11) is what balances it. *What the player learns:* the web is causal and restraint is a move. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* On a derelict, Moment A competes with walking out: a hop away from the locus voids the due-run breach and keeps the finished cut (AT-22), while the abort forfeits the partial, so when the pod is within about 37 tiles (the shortest played tell at the 2 px/tick walk; about 19 tiles at the 1 px/tick carry) leaving tends to beat restraint; the consequence is stated under Moment D, measured by AC-AT-134 and routed to the user (OQ-AT-36).
=== 81
*Moment D, "It's heavy" (the haul under a rising tell; user ruling X3).* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The cut is done and the module comes off the wall; the player lifts it and starts for the pod. Carrying is a stimulus they chose and can hear: the Controller pushes a burden on every tick the cargo is in their hands (`U_BURDEN`, F-26), walking or standing, so a haul is never quiet and standing still with the cargo in hand is not a way to wait the web out: while they hold salvage the web forgets nothing (the decay is suspended, F-5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*. Only salvage counts: a module carried at home, or the player's own kit, adds no burden. Partway along the carry the hull creaks: the cut and the load together took the level across the line (at the placeholders, 318 ticks into a 28-tile carry). The player decides: keep walking and trust that the pod is nearer than the tell is long, or set the module down, go still and let the web lose interest, and come back for it. Setting it down is the lever; the module stays where it fell, and re-taking it needs light, and taking the same module up again straight after an abort grants no fresh grace (the rearm keys on the item, AT-10) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*. *What the player learns:* the web hears what you carry as well as what you do, and 'drop the cargo' is the price of hauling, chosen with warning. **The consequence the rulings leave, stated so the user sees it before the first playable** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: keeping walking to the pod is usually the better answer, because a hop away from a derelict locus voids the due-run breach (AT-22) and keeps everything carried, while setting the module down to abort forfeits the haul for now; when the pod is nearer than the shortest tell is long (about 19 tiles at the 1 px/tick carry for a hauler, about 37 tiles at the 2 px/tick walk for anyone else, PC-15), walking out is close to dominant for any derelict tell, hauling or not, and both restraint aborts and breaches trend toward zero. This follows from two user rulings (the void, OQ-AT-12; the carry burden, X3) and is not reopened here: AC-AT-134 measures it and OQ-AT-36 routes the options to the user.

=== 202
**AT-10. Restraint aborts a tell.** *Rule.* During TELL, after each run's integration: if `L < theta_HOLD` then `below_hold_runs += 1`, else it resets to 0. The tell **aborts to CALM** when `below_hold_runs × 6 ≥ ABORT_HOLD_TICKS` (placeholder 120, run-quantised; the first run under the line counts as run 1), **or** at the first run with `T ≥ breach_due_T` if `L < theta_HOLD` at that run, **or** at that same run if the departure void holds (`locus_vacated`, AT-22; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*). If both are true on the same run the abort wins (one transition). An abort deposits no STRESS, switches no beacon, sets `tell_outcome = ABORTED`, freezes `tell_beat`, leaves `L` unchanged (a knob `ABORT_RELIEF_PM` defaulting to 1000, which means "no relief" and means the abort is unchanged from the ruled behaviour, lets a tuner cap the level at an abort if playtests show chained-abort fatigue) and sets `rearm_until_T = T + TELL_REARM_TICKS` (placeholder 600). **The rearm keys on the item, not on the pickup** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*: while a TELL runs, Attention records in `tell_carry_items` (persisted, AT-1) the `carry_ref` of every seat whose `BURDEN` push it drained (an ordered read of `controller.state`, the same read as `loco_state`, AT-31); after an abort the set is kept until `rearm_until_T`. On any CALM run before `rearm_until_T` that drains a `BURDEN` push from a seat whose `carry_ref` is in the set, `rearm_until_T` is set to that run's `T`, so dropping the cargo to abort and taking the same item up again grants no fresh `TELL_REARM_TICKS` immunity: the next crossing opens a tell at once. A different item leaves the rearm in place. The set is cleared at TELL entry (and refilled during the tell), at BREACH entry (a breached tell sets no rearm) and when the rearm ends. A player who keeps being loud through the tell forfeits the abort; that is intended ("we chose to be loud"). Restraint always costs the partial (Formulas F-15b), and that price is deliberate *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; it is balanced by a breach that has teeth (AT-11), so neither choice dominates. `tell_remaining` published to Save/Load is the time to `breach_due_T`: the conservative direction, because an abort only ends the block early. Two invariants, both lint: **(a) rearm against autosave:** `TELL_REARM_TICKS ≥ AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS` (cited), which guarantees an open soft-gate window between chained aborted tells even under STRICT mode. **(b) abortability at entry:** a player who enters TELL at the highest possible level (`L_CEIL`, AT-5) and then zeroes every player-controlled input (still, beam off, no verbs, any cargo set down) falls under `theta_HOLD` minus a margin `ATT_MARGIN` before `TELL_MIN_TICKS − 6` ticks elapse, at the ring's survivable-dark floor. In words: the tell is a window of agency even at its shortest. The play-level variant, which adds a reaction allowance and evaluates against the shortest draw a player can actually meet, is the registered formula `abortability_play` (AT-8, CQ-4; Formulas F-15b).
=== 264
**AT-22. Dormancy and pod hop *(Web Map & Transit is designed; its WM-26 sentence contradicts the confirmed void, and a hard rewrite is routed, C28, OQ-AT-35)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *Rule.* Dormant sections give no stimuli and hold no ledger. `IN_POD` holds the departure ring (AT-6); a hop between two ring-1 loci (the MVP's only kind, HOME and a ring-1 derelict) holds `held_ring` 1 throughout, so `B` does not change (Web Map ASK-A1). The pod's running light is cosmetic presentation, not authored as an emitter (WM-26): it is not an eligible tell region (AT-20) and not a light stimulus (AT-4). The DOCK_STATUS glow on the docked pod's dock-room prop is a different object: it is a real emitter (Emitter EM-3), so it is a light stimulus (F-3) and an unswitchable one (AT-6, F-16), but never a tell carrier (AT-20) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. A pod hop does **not** interrupt a TELL (the clock, the bed and the beats run through the hop), but it can **void the due-run breach** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(creative-director ruling on OQ-AT-12; **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): the void is confirmed**)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: at TELL entry the living seats inside `locus_body` are recorded as `tell_occupants_at_entry`. At the first run with `T ≥ breach_due_T`, if the locus body is **not** the home-ship body, `tell_occupants_at_entry` is non-empty and **no living seat's `actor_section` is in the recorded `locus_body`** (everyone who was in it has left, by pod or otherwise; a recorded seat that died inside the body or whose position cannot be resolved still counts as present, and a seat in the pod counts as gone, the `occ_gone` rule of F-14 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), the tell ends as an abort: TELL → CALM, `tell_outcome = ABORTED`, no STRESS, no beacon, `rearm_until_T` set, the release cue plays (`locus_vacated`, F-14 third clause). The test runs against the recorded `locus_body` **before** any dormancy fallback, and during the TELL the fallback is suppressed from the first run at which `locus_vacated` holds (AT-14), so a departed, dormant derelict is never turned into a breach on the home ship the player just escaped to, neither at the due run nor on any run between the hop and it. Reason: a fallback that punishes the hop contradicts the Player Fantasy ('leave, and the web lets go'), punishes the game's natural escape verb in a lethal-breach game (Horror HE-F16) and teaches players not to flee during a tell, against Pillar 3's 'a price chosen with full warning'. If a living seat stays in the locus body the breach proceeds on that body unchanged (co-op: the staying seat faces it; the departing seat is safe unless the body is welded to theirs). A home-ship locus is not voidable: there is no escape by pod from a breach centred on the home ship (Moment B variant). **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), OQ-AT-12 (2):** a home-ship-locus tell is NOT escapable by hopping to a derelict; 'the lights you left on' is the price *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. **Reply to Web Map ASK-A4 (WM-26b, OQ-WM-42): declined** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: Attention does not hold the TELL-to-STRESS transfer while no seat is aboard the home body; a home-ship-locus breach proceeds as ruled, because holding it until someone returns would turn the hop into a way to defer a home breach, which the ruling above forbids. With the void, a hop away from a non-home locus never moves STRESS onto the home ship, so WM-26's sentence 'the due-run breach STRESSes the home ship' describes behaviour this document no longer has; the home-ship locus with nobody aboard is E-73. A locus body that held no living seat at TELL entry (a lit, unoccupied, berthed derelict, WM-21) has nothing to void and breaches as before, ending under X10. BREACH ends when the last living occupant recorded at BREACH entry (`locus_occupants_at_entry`) leaves a locus body that is not the home-ship; a player who was never inside does not trigger it, and while any recorded occupant is still inside the clause is false. **Departure is derivable now** from Ship Body's `actor_section(actor_id)`: `locus_occupants_at_entry` is non-empty and no living seat's `actor_section` is in the recorded `locus_body` (a set of section ids), equivalently `body_of_actor(actor_id) ≠ body_of(locus_section_id)` for every living seat, plus the persisted `occ_gone` bits for recorded seats that are dead or cannot be resolved (F-14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, which makes the rule testable before Web Map exists; Web Map's pod-hop notification (named by Web Map; Save/Load also consumes one, SL event triggers) is the eventual signal and must be repeated by Web Map. If the locus section is cut away or goes dormant mid-event, the locus falls back per AT-14 and the locus body is recomputed (never as the consequence of a departure, which the void above resolves first); STRESS already armed on a cut-away section lapses on its own hold. **A death in the pod** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(user ruling D60, 2026-10-27)*: statuses run in the pod (Suit's air, cell, thermal and counters, and the Sanity and Attention clocks, all keep running) and a seat that dies there is the Controller's `DEAD`; Attention reads that through `loco_state` (AT-31), so a seat in the pod is living until then, a dead one stops counting for `B` and for the pod hold, and if it was the last recorded occupant of a non-home locus its section had already left `locus_body`, so the departure clauses already hold. **Ordering in BREACH:** the departure test above is evaluated against the recorded `locus_body` before any dormancy fallback in the same run, so a pod departure that empties a non-home locus ends the breach and no fallback occurs (WM:87, Moment 2; E-27).

content.content: - **If the carrier hops home with the instance held after a tell on the derelict (EC-BS-63)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*: the burden stops when the seat enters the pod. It is pushed only while the salvage is held aboard the non-home locus body where it was taken, never `IN_POD` and never aboard the home body (delegated ruling R5, 'never to carrying at home', read with the creative-director's lean on the re-review; in the fiction, *the web hears the taking at the wreck*, BS-15), and the level then decays in the pod as usual. On the reference carry the tell is resolved before the pod arrives (from the tell's opening, the carry ahead, the console and the pod leg run-quantised to 948 ticks take 2,004 ticks, more than `TELL_DRAW_HI` 1800), by the departure void or the abort (AT-22, AT-10); the level arrives home at 75 percent of `ATT_THRESHOLD` (4,511,793 mAU) with the beam and the lit home ship feeding it in the pod, or 62 percent (3,734,036) with no pod intake, and stands at 4,389,820 or 3,796,361 mAU at the install after the 486-tick home carry: below `theta_HOLD`, with no home-ship tell (AC-BS-123 (e)). Were the burden to run in the pod and at home, the decay would stay suspended, the voided tell's item-keyed rearm would end on the first CALM run that drains the same item's push (AT-10), and a home-ship tell that no hop can void (D46) would open at once on every successful sortie that kept its module; that is why the scope is keyed on place. A shorter carry whose tell is still running when the pod arrives home is voided at its due run all the same, because every recorded seat has left the locus body (AT-22). Attention's AT-3 keys the push on the pickup locus and says 'never for carrying at home'; this GDD reads that as a gate on the holder's current section and asks Attention to state it, `IN_POD` included, in AT-3 and F-26, and the Controller to declare the push (OQ-BS-30, ASK-BS-A2 (a), ASK-BS-C2) (D.2; AT-22, AT-10).

PATH = sys.argv[1]
EDITS = sys.argv[2]

    s = s.replace(old, new, 1)
